question: Secondary glaucomas can be classified mechanistically into open-angle and closed-angle types: open-angle secondary glaucomas involve increased trabecular resistance (e.g. pigment dispersion, pseudoexfoliation, steroid-induced), while closed-angle types involve mechanical closure of the iridocorneal angle (e.g. neovascular, phacomorphic).

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. Applying this framework lets you reason about unfamiliar secondary glaucomas: identify whether the angle is open or closed on gonioscopy, then deduce the mechanism. This is more durable than memorising individual diagnoses.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. The mechanistic scaffold is powerful: in open-angle secondary glaucomas, the angle is open but outflow is impeded (blocked trabecular pores from pigment, pseudoexfoliative material, or steroid-induced glycosaminoglycan accumulation). In closed-angle types, the angle itself is physically closed — by neovascular membranes, a swollen lens, or synechiae.
